methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $43M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
FleetZero is a Series A transportation company that has raised $43M to date. The comparable universe consists of 8 private firms in the transportation sector, including later-stage peers such as Rivian and The Boring Company, though no direct public market comparables exist for this stage and subsector.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable valuation approach here. Using FleetZero's $43M total raised as a baseline proxy for post-money valuation, a 2.0x step-up multiplier—standard for progression from Series A to subsequent institutional rounds—yields an implied valuation of $86M. This method reflects observed investor step-up patterns but assumes continued capital availability and execution on milestones.

The peer-median approach cannot be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting the three-datapoint threshold. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material estimation error given the heterogeneity of transportation subsectors and funding profiles.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $73M (low) to $99M (high), with a median of $86M. This range rests on a single methodology, creating notable uncertainty around the point estimate. Key risks include the limited comp visibility at this stage in transportation, execution risk on Series A product-market fit, and the capital intensity typical of the sector. External validation through Series A term-sheet data would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
